summary: Reproduced a randomly initialized Qwen3 sequence-classification bias when a checkpoint omitted score.bias. The classifier bias is now initialized to zero, retaining bias-free logits for standard checkpoints while the existing loader still preserves an explicit checkpoint bias.

tests.what_was_measured: Regression reproduced on the recorded base: the missing-bias case differed from an independent bias-free linear reference in all 6 logits, with maximum absolute error 0.3341083526611328. Raw output: reports/j-1d9ad3ee2f2e/raw/failing_before.txt
CPU regression passed exact comparisons for both a missing score.bias and an explicit nonzero score.bias. Raw output: reports/j-1d9ad3ee2f2e/raw/passing_after.txt

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-1d9ad3ee2f2e/venv/bin/python - [inline ROCm head-loading and logit-parity script]
tests.what_was_measured: On one AMD Instinct MI355X, both missing-bias and explicit-bias GPU logits exactly matched independent torch.nn.functional.linear references (rtol=0, atol=0; maximum absolute error 0.0). Raw output and method: reports/j-1d9ad3ee2f2e/raw/gpu_numerical.txt

gpu_execution.evidence: PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 with HIP 7.2.26015 executed the classification head on the sole visible AMD Instinct MI355X; exact parity was observed for bias-free and explicit-bias references.

remaining_limitations: Validation isolates the classification head and its real load_weights path by replacing the unrelated transformer backbone with nn.Identity. It does not run a full checkpoint-backed server or transformer forward. No native source changed, so no native rebuild was needed.
